newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bank earnings up 10 pct or better in Q4.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bank earnings up 10 pct or better in Q4.

text.p: A number of U.S. bank holding companies Wednesday posted fourth quarter earnings that generally improved on year-earlier results by about 10 percent or more.
The results were close to Wall Street expectations and credit quality appeared good throughout the industry with ample reserves for problem loans.

Credit card chargeoffs continued to rise creating the only blemish on a generally good quarter for the banks, but analysts said credit card problems may soon ease. Even with the rise in the chargeoffs, the card business remains profitable.

"Clearly the credit card losses have continued to creep up but not spike up," said Michael Mayo, analyst at Lehman Brothers. Overall, he said the earnings were a continuation of "steady upward progress" that has been occurring for the last couple of years.

Frank Barkocy, analyst at Josephthal, Lyon & Ross said that banks are taking corrective steps to deal with rising loss rates in credit cards but "like a supertanker you don't turn it around immediately."

"I think overall earnings were good, and share buybacks have helped and will continue to be a factor in earnings for the group in 1997," Barkocy said. He noted that overall asset quality was good at the banks he tracks.

Boston-based Fleet Financial Group Inc reported fourth quarter operating earnings rose 12 percent from a year ago to $1.05 per share. Fleet, which has been digesting two big acquisitions, said fourth quarter operating earnings rose 16 percent to $302 million.
Separately, Fleet announced plans to buy back up to 20 million shares of common stock and to sell three units.
San Francisco-based BankAmerica Corp reported fourth quarter earnings per share rose 10 percent from a year ago to $1.92 diluted.

Catherine Murray, analyst at J.P. Morgan & Co, said BankAmerica had a "very solid quarter." She noted that BankAmerica repurchased 4.76 milion shares in the fourth quarter, not quite as much as she expected. But the analyst added that BankAmerica is in the midst of a continuing restructuring.
Murray said Winston-Salem, N.C.-based Wachovia Corp also had a good quarter. Chargeoffs for loans overall rose, but in line with expectations.
First Chicago NBD Corp reported fourth-quarter operating earnings rose 19 percent from a year ago to $1.14 per share diluted.

First Chicago, which is one of the biggest players among U.S. banks in credit card lending, reported that the chargeoff ratio for bad credit card loans rose to 6.7 percent from 5.9 percent in the third quarter.
Raphael Soifer, analyst at Brown Brothers Harriman, noted that the credit card business still produced record profits for First Chicago NBD in the fourth quarter.
First Chicago repurchased 7.3 million of its common shares in the fourth quarter.

Pittsburgh-based PNC Bank Corp reported fourth quarter earnings were $0.79 per share diluted compared to a loss reported in the fourth quarter of 1995. For the year, PNC's earnings were $2.87 per share diluted compared to $1.19 per share diluted in 1995.
Elsewhere, Republic New York Corp, ranked among the 20-largest U.S. bank holding companies, reported fourth quarter earnings rose 18 percent to $1.82 per share.
U.S. bank earnings reported earlier in the week and a few last week also showed no surprises, and analysts are fairly confident earnings still to come in the current cycle will be generally good.
